source.title: Primary School Education Curriculum Design — Social Studies, Grade 6
source.notes: Read in full via the Read tool (no pages param). ISBN 978-9914-724-91-2, First Published 2017, Revised 2024. Grade 6 is Upper Primary. 5 strands / 22 sub-strands / 90 total suggested lessons. Content is regional (Eastern Africa: Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan, Somalia, Ethiopia) rather than Kenya-only for Strands 1-3; Strands 4-5 (Political Systems, Governance) are Kenya-specific except 4.1 (Buganda/Nyamwezi traditional government, explicitly named) and 4.2 (East African Community). Appendix I covers CSL guidelines (Social Studies hosts the one annual integrated CSL activity at Upper Primary) — practical/not a generated-skill target, same treatment as other grades' CSL sub-strand.

subStrands.name: 1.1 Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify the countries of Eastern Africa on a map
Describe the position and size of countries in Eastern Africa
Use latitudes and longitudes to locate places on a map
Appreciate the unity of Eastern African countries
keyInquiryQuestions: How do you determine the position of countries in Eastern Africa?
learningExperiences: Identify countries in Eastern Africa on a map, and share in class
Locate, in groups, the position of countries in Eastern Africa using an atlas/appropriate media
Use digital devices to establish the sizes in square kilometres of countries in Eastern Africa
Draw, colour and display the map of Eastern Africa in class
In pairs, identify latitudes and longitudes of Eastern Africa using appropriate media
Practise locating places on a map using latitudes and longitudes
linkedLearningAreas: Science and Technology — using digital devices to locate positions of countries based on latitudes and longitudes
Creative Arts — drawing latitudes and longitudes on a sketch map of Eastern Africa
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Rubric only formally assesses physical-feature/climate/historic-built-environment/vegetation-map abilities for this sub-strand's group, not a standalone lat/long rubric row — but the outcome itself ('use latitudes and longitudes to locate places on a map') and the Suggested Learning Experiences' explicit lat/long practice bullet make it squarely testable.
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Critical thinking (differences between latitudes and longitudes)
Citizenship (singing the East African Community Anthem)

subStrands.name: 1.2 Main Physical Features in Eastern Africa

keyInquiryQuestions: How can we conserve physical features found in our locality?

scopeNotes: include: physical feature categories are explicitly named — volcanic mountains, bloc (block) mountains, rift valleys, lakes, plains
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Exceeds tier rewards describing the importance of physical features 'with details' — recall of the feature category alone (e.g. 'mountain') is not enough; a branch should require naming the formation process or a specific example.
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Environmental Education (conserving physical features in the locality)

scopeNotes: include: the three classical Eastern African language-group classifications (Bantu, Nilotic, Cushitic) are the standard reference point, though the source text itself leaves 'selected language groups' open rather than naming a fixed list — treat as an explicit classification-by-language-family outcome
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Exceeds tier for describing migration/settlement effects rewards doing so 'with details' — a branch should distinguish cause (why a group migrated) from effect (what happened after settlement), not conflate them.

subStrands.name: 4.1 Traditional Forms of Government

English/Kiswahili/KSL — role-playing scenarios depicting aspects of good governance in society
scopeNotes: include: exactly two named traditional governments to compare — the Buganda (a centralised kingdom, whose parliament/council is explicitly named 'the Lukiiko') and the Nyamwezi (a decentralised, chiefdom-based society); this sub-strand's fact pool is inherently narrower than most others since only two societies are named — do not invent additional named traditional kingdoms not present in the source
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Exceeds tier for comparing the two governments rewards doing so 'with examples' — a branch should require a genuine compare/contrast (centralised kingship vs. decentralised chieftaincy), not just describing each in isolation.
